NASA’s flagship X-ray observatory, in service since 1999. Resolution roughly 25× better than any previous X-ray telescope, allowing direct imaging of black-hole accretion disks, supernova remnants, and the hot gas threading galaxy clusters.
Infrared Great Observatory; 16 years of data
One of NASA's four Great Observatories
Iconic visible/UV space telescope; 5 servicing missions

NASA's X-ray eye. Its extreme elliptical orbit swings from 9,942 km to 133,600 km — one third of the way to the Moon. This takes it outside Earth's radiation belts for long, clean observations. Sees black holes, neutron stars, supernovae — the violent high-energy universe invisible to optical telescopes.
